title: Who are the “two witnesses” of Revelation 11:3, and where and when do they prophesy?
summary: Revelation 11:3 says “I will give power unto my two witnesses, and they shall prophesy a thousand two hundred and threescore days”. The verses do not name them, say whether they are two persons or two figures of something else, or say when the days fall.
text: KJV Revelation 11:3: “I will give power unto my two witnesses, and they shall prophesy a thousand two hundred and threescore days”. Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) Revelation 11:3: τοῖς δυσὶν μάρτυσίν μου [to my two witnesses]; the Textus Receptus text served prints the same words. KJV Revelation 11:4: “These are the two olive trees, and the two candlesticks”. Greek: αἱ δύο ἐλαῖαι [the two olive trees]. KJV Revelation 11:7: “when they shall have finished their testimony, the beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit shall make war against them”. KJV Revelation 11:8: “in the street of the great city”. KJV Revelation 11:12: “they ascended up to heaven in a cloud”. KJV Zechariah 4:14: “These are the two anointed ones, that stand by the Lord of the whole earth”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/66/11/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/66/11/.
reasoning: The passage gives the witnesses’ number (two), their speaker (“my”), the length of their prophesying, their dress, their death, their rising and their ascent, and it says of them that they are “the two olive trees, and the two candlesticks”. It does not give a name or a time. It does not say whether the “great city” of 11:8 is a place on a map or a figure, or whether the days are counted as days. The two olive trees recall the two “anointed ones” of Zechariah 4:14, which does not name them either. Readings that have been held include two named prophets of the Old Testament returning, two persons of the last days who are not named, and two figures standing for the church’s witness or for the Law and the Prophets. The verses quoted state none of these and the record does not choose among them.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The question is limited to Revelation 11:3–12, with Zechariah 4:14 as the verse the picture of the two olive trees recalls. The record does not say which reading is right and does not claim that no other passage of the Bible says more. The Greek quoted is Tischendorf’s eighth edition as served by bolls.life, checked against the Textus Receptus text served there. The Greek New Testament wording is Tischendorf’s eighth edition as served by bolls.life (TISCH), compared with the Textus Receptus text served there (TR); neither is a critical apparatus.

title: Who are the hundred and forty and four thousand “sealed” (Revelation 7:4, 14:1–4), and are they the “great multitude” of 7:9?
summary: Revelation 7:4 says “there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel”, and 7:9 then describes “a great multitude, which no man could number”. Revelation 14:1–4 has a hundred and forty and four thousand “redeemed from the earth”. The verses do not say whether the group of 7:4 and the group of 14:1 are one, or whether the multitude of 7:9 is the same group seen differently or a second group.
text: KJV Revelation 7:4: “there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel”. Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) Revelation 7:4: ἐκ πάσης φυλῆς υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ [of every tribe of the sons of Israel]; the Textus Receptus text served prints the same words. KJV Revelation 7:9: “a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations”. KJV Revelation 14:1: “with him an hundred forty and four thousand”. KJV Revelation 14:3: “which were redeemed from the earth”. KJV Revelation 14:4: “These are they which were not defiled with women; for they are virgins”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/66/7/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/66/7/.
reasoning: Chapter 7 gives the number once (7:4) and then lists twelve tribes with twelve thousand each; “after this” (7:9) the seer sees a multitude from every nation that no one could number. Chapter 14 names a hundred and forty and four thousand again, “redeemed from the earth” and “from among men”. The passages do not say whether the number is a count or a figure, whether “the tribes of the children of Israel” are the tribes by descent or a name for a wider people, whether the multitude of 7:9 is the same people seen after the sealing, or whether the words about “women” and “virgins” in 14:4 are a literal description. Readings that have been held include a literal number of Israelites, a figure for the whole company of the redeemed, and a distinct group within a larger one. The verses quoted state none of these and the record does not choose among them.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The question is limited to Revelation 7:1–17 and 14:1–5. The two groups are not said to be the same in either chapter, and are not said to be different. The record does not say which reading is right and does not claim that no other passage of the Bible says more. title: “The number of a man” (Revelation 13:18): whose name is the number of the beast?
summary: Revelation 13:18 says “Let him that hath understanding count the number of the beast: for it is the number of a man; and his number is Six hundred threescore and six”, and 13:17 speaks of “the name of the beast, or the number of his name”. The verses ask the reader to count, and they do not give the name the number is made from, or say whose name it is.
text: KJV Revelation 13:18: “Let him that hath understanding count the number of the beast: for it is the number of a man”. Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) Revelation 13:18: ψηφισάτω τὸν ἀριθμὸν τοῦ θηρίου, ἀριθμὸς γὰρ ἀνθρώπου ἐστίν [let him count the number of the beast, for it is the number of a man]; the Textus Receptus text served prints the same words. KJV Revelation 13:17: “the number of his name”. Greek: τὸν ἀριθμὸν τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ [the number of his name]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/66/13/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/66/13/.
reasoning: The verse tells the reader to count, says the number is that of “a man” and gives the number. It does not give the name, the language in which the name is to be counted, or the person. The previous verse ties the number to “the name of the beast”, so the verses imply that a name stands behind the number, but they do not give it. Readings that have been held include a named ruler of the first century, a name or title in Hebrew or Greek letters, a figure for incompleteness or opposition to God, and a person of the last days not yet named. The verses quoted state none of these and the record does not choose among them.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The question is limited to Revelation 13:17–18. The record does not discuss readings of the numeral in other manuscripts. It does not say which reading is right and does not claim that no other passage of the Bible says more.
